name: Cavitary Myiasis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Parasitological Diagnostic Criteria for Cavitary Myiasis

criteria.description: Identification of fly larvae within a body cavity by direct visualization or extraction
Presence of localized symptoms consistent with tissue invasion in a body cavity (e.g., nasal, oral, aural, urogenital, or pulmonary)
Imaging studies demonstrating cavitary lesions or foreign bodies consistent with larvae
Histopathological confirmation of larval tissue invasion or associated inflammatory response

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of larvae within a body cavity confirmed by direct visualization or extraction plus compatible clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by parasitological confirmation; imaging and histopathology aid in complex cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible motile larvae within body cavity
pathognomonic.notes: Direct visualization of larvae is diagnostic

pathognomonic.symptomName: Foul-smelling serosanguinous discharge from affected cavity
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic malodorous discharge due to tissue necrosis

common.symptomName: Localized tissue ulceration within affected cavity
common.notes: Ulcerative lesions caused by larval feeding

common.symptomName: Pruritus or irritation at infestation site
Edema and erythema surrounding cavity opening

occasional.symptomName: Epistaxis or nasal obstruction (if nasal cavity involved)
Otalgia or hearing impairment (if aural cavity involved)
Cough or hemoptysis (if pulmonary cavity involved)
searchTerms: lung cavity causing cough and bleeding

occasional.symptomName: Dysuria or hematuria (if urogenital cavity involved)

rare.symptomName: Sepsis secondary to extensive tissue invasion
Neurological symptoms due to intracranial extension (rare complication)

laboratory: Identification of larvae or larval fragments in discharge or tissue samples
Elevated inflammatory markers in blood tests if secondary infection present
imaging: CT or MRI showing cavitary lesions with possible moving foreign bodies
Ultrasound may detect larvae in accessible cavities
other: Histopathology revealing larval structures and associated tissue necrosis
Endoscopic visualization of larvae within cavities

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of larvae on direct examination
Different etiology with inflammatory mucosal changes
Rapidly progressive soft tissue infection without larvae

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating possible intracranial extension
references: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Myiasis. CDC Yellow Book 2024.
Gupta S, et al. Cavitary myiasis: clinical features and management. J Infect Dis. 2022;225(4):678-685.
